findings.explanation: QueryParser.parse (new entry point) builds SQL text by interpolating attacker-controlled identifiers directly into the SQL string via f-strings, with no allowlist. The `q` request parameter (and `q.df`) is parsed by pyparsing into tokens whose field names, attribute names and field identifiers are inserted verbatim into the SQL: e.g. `f'"{self.tokens.field[0]}" ILIKE %({p})s'`, `f'"{tokens_attr}"::jsonb ->>%({p_key})s ...'`, and `f'"{self.tokens.fieldname or self.tokens.field[0]}"'`. The `default_field` argument (from `params.get('q.df')`) is also spliced in via `sql.replace('__default_field__', default_field)`. These identifiers are not validated against a fixed allowlist, so an attacker can inject arbitrary SQL through the field/attribute names. The resulting `parsed_query` is placed into `Query.where` (utils.py:152) and executed with `WHERE {query.where}` (base.py:364), where the interpolated identifiers are not bound parameters.

findings.suggested_fix: Validate every interpolated identifier (field name, attribute name, and default_field) against a strict allowlist of known column/attribute names before embedding it in the SQL string, or rewrite the query to use only bound parameters for values and a fixed set of whitelisted identifiers. Custom backends example
=======================

Provided example consists of a database backend based on standard PostgreSQL backend.

It has a very basic functionality, adding an attribute to the alert before storing it
in the database. This functionality can be achieved using plugins, it is just an example.

Custom backends must provide a class named 'Backend' that implements `alerta.database.base.Backend`.

The module providing that class must be referenced as an 'alerta.database.backends' entry-point in
python package setup.

```
   ...
    entry_points={
        'alerta.database.backends': [
            'custom = package'
        ]
    }
    ...
```

To use the custom database backend, the name used for the entry-point has to be used as schema in
`DATABASE_URL` configuration setting:

```
DATABASE_URL = "custom://user@db_server/monitoring?connect_timeout=10&application_name=alerta"
```

configuration:

```
DEBUG=True
```

Custom backends example
=======================

Provided example consists of a database backend based on standard PostgreSQL backend.

It has a very basic functionality, adding an attribute to the alert before storing it
in the database. This functionality can be achieved using plugins, it is just an example.

Custom backends must provide a class named 'Backend' that implements `alerta.database.base.Backend`.

The module providing that class must be referenced as an 'alerta.database.backends' entry-point in
python package setup.

```
   ...
    entry_points={
        'alerta.database.backends': [
            'custom = package'
        ]
    }
    ...
```

To use the custom database backend, the name used for the entry-point has to be used as schema in
`DATABASE_URL` configuration setting:

```
DATABASE_URL = "custom://user@db_server/monitoring?connect_timeout=10&application_name=alerta"
```
